title: A. Setup
text:
This setup guide will help you install the necessary tools and dependencies to run the Climate Data Cube workshop code on your local machine.
Because the workshop code is designed to run in a Linux environment, we will use Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2) on Windows. If you are using macOS or Linux or have WSL installed, you can skip the WSL installation and use your native/WSL terminal.

title: A. Setup
text:
1. Install WSL2 and Ubuntu

Open the Windows Start menu, search for PowerShell, and choose Run as administrator.
Run the following command in Windows PowerShell:

wsl --install -d Ubuntu

Restart Windows if prompted.
Launch Ubuntu from the Start menu and wait for first-time initialization.
Create your Ubuntu username and password when prompted. Password characters are not displayed while typing.

Check installation in Windows PowerShell:
wsl --list --verbose
You should see Ubuntu with VERSION equal to 2. If Ubuntu is version 1, use:
wsl --set-version Ubuntu 2
If wsl --install displays help instead of installing, try wsl --list --online, then wsl --install -d Ubuntu. If installation is blocked by policy or virtualization, contact your IT administrator. Do not attempt to bypass institutional restrictions.
Official guide: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install

title: A. Setup
text:
2. Install Visual Studio Code
If you do not have VS Code installed, follow these steps:

Download VS Code for Windows: https://code.visualstudio.com/download.
Install VS Code on Windows (not inside Ubuntu).
Open VS Code → Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X). Install:

WSL (Microsoft)
Python (Microsoft)
Jupyter (Microsoft)


Official WSL + VS Code guide: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/wsl

title: A. Setup
text:
3. Prepare Ubuntu and system dependencies
Open the Ubuntu terminal from the Windows Start menu and run:
sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y \
  git wget curl ca-certificates \
  cdo python3 python3-venv python3-pip
Verify:
cdo -V
git --version
python3 --version
wget --version | head -n 1

Why CDO? CDO performs the controlled spatial processing in this workshop: clipping and remapping.

title: A. Setup
text:
4. Install uv (Python dependency manager)
Inside Ubuntu, install uv using the official installer:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Restart the Ubuntu terminal or refresh the shell configuration (as instructed by the installer). Verify:
uv --version
Documentation: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/

title: A. Setup
text:
5. Clone the Repository
Keep the repository inside the Linux home directory for better file performance (for example, ~/projects/), rather than under /mnt/c/.
mkdir -p ~/projects
cd ~/projects

git clone https://github.com/khizerzakir/tutorial-repo.git
cd <YOUR-REPOSITORY> ## replace with the actual repository name
Open the Linux folder in VS Code:
code .
The first launch may install the VS Code Server in WSL. Check the lower-left corner of VS Code for WSL: Ubuntu. Open Terminal → New Terminal: it should be a Linux shell.

title: A. Setup
section: 6. Install the project’s Python dependencies (choose uv or pip)
text:
6. Install the project’s Python dependencies (choose uv or pip)

Option A — uv (recommended if installed)
From the repository root in the VS Code WSL terminal:
uv sync --locked
For notebooks, only if the project defines a notebook optional dependency group:
uv sync --locked --extra notebook
If --extra notebook is not defined, follow the repository’s pyproject.toml instructions instead. uv.lock should be committed so students resolve the same dependency versions. Confirm the environment:
uv run python -c "import xarray, zarr; print('xarray and zarr: OK')"


Option B — pip with requirements.txt (no uv required)
If you do not have uv, use the system-provided Python and create an isolated virtual environment. Run these commands inside Ubuntu, from the GitLab repository root:
# Install Python virtual-environment support if needed
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv python3-pip

# Create and activate a project-local environment
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install the pinned project requirements
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# Confirm that key libraries are available
python -c "import xarray, zarr; print('xarray and zarr: OK')"
For notebooks, check whether requirements.txt includes ipykernel and jupyterlab. If not, install them in the activated environment:
python -m pip install ipykernel jupyterlab
python -m ipykernel install --user --name lsasaf-cube --display-name "Python (LSA SAF Cube)"

Important: Keep the virtual environment activated for subsequent terminal commands. When you open a new Ubuntu terminal, run source .venv/bin/activate again. Do not use sudo pip install. The requirements.txt must be committed to GitLab and kept consistent with the tested uv.lock; pip does not read uv.lock automatically.

title: A. Setup
text:
7. Set up LSA SAF credentials
Follow the instructions in the repository’s README.md to obtain a username and password for the LSA SAF Data Service. You will need these credentials to download sample data.
Create a local credentials file (never commit it):
cp .env.example .env
Open .env in VS Code and enter the account details obtained from the LSA SAF Data Service:
USERNAME=your_lsa_saf_username
PASSWORD=your_lsa_saf_password
Register or access your account at https://datalsasaf.lsasvcs.ipma.pt/. Ensure .env is listed in .gitignore. Do not share .env in screenshots, commits, or submissions.

title: A. Setup
text:
10. Troubleshooting







Problem
Suggested action




wsl not recognized
Check Windows version and Windows updates; consult the official WSL guide.


WSL installation blocked
Ask university IT about virtualization and Windows feature permissions.


code: command not found
Install VS Code on Windows with the WSL extension; reopen Ubuntu and try code ..


cdo: command not found
Run sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y cdo inside Ubuntu.


uv: command not found
Restart Ubuntu terminal and follow the PATH instructions from the uv installer.


Permission denied for .sh
Use bash scripts/NAME.sh; ensure scripts use Unix LF line endings.


config.txt or grid.txt missing
Check the preprocessing wrapper’s working directory and configuration paths.


No NetCDF files found
Confirm the preceding stage completed and files are under data/raw/ or data/interim/ as expected.


Jupyter kernel not found
In VS Code, select the interpreter at .venv/bin/python and ensure notebook dependencies are installed.


Slow processing under /mnt/c
Move the repository into ~/projects/ in Ubuntu.

INTERIM="/home/khizer/scientific_contributions/tutorial-repo/data/interim/2010/01/NETCDF4_LSASAF_MSG_METREF_MSG-Disk_201001010000_processed.nc"


import xarray as xr
import numpy as np

for path in [RAW, INTERIM]:
    print(f"\n{path}")
    with xr.open_dataset(path, decode_cf=True, mask_and_scale=True) as ds:
        print(ds.sizes)
        for name, da in ds.data_vars.items():
            if da.dtype.kind in "iuf":
                valid = int(np.isfinite(da).sum().compute())
                print(name, "valid:", valid, "/", da.size)
                if valid:
                    print("min/max:", float(da.min().compute()), float(da.max().compute()))

The code
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Create a compressed, sharded Zarr v3 cube from interim NetCDF files."""

from pathlib import Path
import shutil

import xarray as xr
import zarr
from packaging.version import Version


if Version(zarr.__version__) < Version("3.0"):
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"Zarr >= 3.0 is required, but {zarr.__version__} is installed. "
        "Run this script with the project environment, for example: "
        "`uv run python code/build_zarr_cube.py`."
    )

from zarr.codecs import BloscCodec


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
INTERIM = ROOT / "data" / "interim"
OUTPUT = ROOT / "data" / "zarr" / "metref_sample_1month.zarr"

# Intended access: time slices / maps. Tune after benchmarking your real data.
INNER_CHUNKS = {"time": 1, "lat": 256, "lon": 256}
SHARD_CHUNKS = {"time": 10, "lat": 512, "lon": 512}
COMPRESSOR = BloscCodec(cname="zstd", clevel=5, shuffle="shuffle")


def main() -> int:
    files = sorted(INTERIM.rglob("*.nc"))
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No NetCDF files found under {INTERIM}")

    print(f"Opening {len(files)} NetCDF files")
    ds = xr.open_mfdataset(
        files,
        combine="by_coords",
        parallel=False,
        chunks="auto",
        engine="h5netcdf",
        data_vars="minimal",
        coords="minimal",
        compat="override",
    )

    # Use the input's actual dimension names; rename here if needed, e.g. y/x.
    missing = (set(INNER_CHUNKS) | set(SHARD_CHUNKS)) - set(ds.dims)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expected dimensions {sorted(missing)} are missing. "
            f"Found {dict(ds.sizes)}; update the chunk settings or rename dimensions."
        )
    if "time" in ds.coords:
        ds = ds.sortby("time")

    # Dask writes one complete shard task at a time. Each shard holds multiple
    # independently compressed inner chunks, reducing object/file counts.
    ds = ds.chunk(SHARD_CHUNKS)
    encoding = {}
    for name, da in ds.data_vars.items():
        if da.dtype.kind not in "iufcb":  # leave strings/objects to xarray defaults
            continue
        dims = da.dims
        inner = tuple(min(INNER_CHUNKS.get(dim, da.sizes[dim]), da.sizes[dim]) for dim in dims)
        shard = tuple(min(SHARD_CHUNKS.get(dim, inner[i]), da.sizes[dim]) for i, dim in enumerate(dims))
        encoding[name] = {
            "chunks": inner,
            "shards": shard,
            "compressors": [COMPRESSOR],
        }

    OUTPUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if OUTPUT.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT)

    print(ds)
    ds.to_zarr(
        OUTPUT,
        mode="w",
        zarr_format=3,
        consolidated=False,
        encoding=encoding,
        align_chunks=True,
    )
    print(f"Wrote Zarr v3 cube: {OUTPUT}")

    # Validate metadata and compute only a tiny sample, not the full cube.
    check = xr.open_zarr(OUTPUT, consolidated=False)
    var = next(iter(check.data_vars))
    sample = check[var]
    indexers = {dim: slice(0, 1 if dim == "time" else 64) for dim in sample.dims}
    value = sample.isel(indexers).mean().compute().item()
    print(f"Validation OK: {var} sample mean = {value}")
    ds.close()
    check.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
